ask: C11, no dependencies. lines.c: Bresenham line drawing with Cohen-Sutherland clipping to a viewport, midpoint circle and filled circle, an 8-bit framebuffer struct with putpixel bounds checks, and a PGM dump. main draws a clipped test pattern. write the file.
prose:
`lines.c` is written and ready. Build and run:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -O2 -o lines lines.c -lm
./lines > out.pgm
```

Open `out.pgm` with any PGM viewer (Preview on macOS, GIMP, `feh`, `eog`, etc.). You should see a 512×512 image with:

- a dark grey field
- a dim viewport border at ±64px inset from each edge
- a 36-spoke starburst clipped to the viewport
- a faint grid clipped at both the viewport and the outer lines
- two full diagonals, clipped to the viewport rectangle
- eight concentric outline circles centered on the frame
- four filled circles sitting on the viewport corners (partially outside, so the bounds check trims them)
- four smaller filled circles inside at ±100px from centre
- two short segments in the bottom-right and top-left corners that are entirely outside the viewport and produce no pixels inside it — confirming the trivial-reject path

The `cs_clip` / `draw_line` / `draw_circle` / `draw_filled_circle` / `fb_write_pgm` APIs are all self-contained and can be pulled into any C11 project as-is.
